deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of the Dirichlet-principle section of Riemann's 1851 dissertation (Grundlagen ..., Art. 17). There he justifies the restriction that the comparison function λ may not approach a discontinuous function γ (g) arbitrarily closely while keeping L finite. The previous page sets up the situation. Near a line of discontinuity of γ, use coordinates s (arc length along the line) and p (signed normal distance), with κ the curvature (positive when concave toward p>0). The area element is (1-κp) ds dp. T' is the strip p2(s) < p < p1(s), with p1 ≥ 0 ≥ p2. On it λ is free; on its boundary λ = γ, with values γ1 at p1 and γ2 at p2.

Implicit core estimate (mine, standard, and stated in the printed Art. 17). For fixed s, Cauchy–Schwarz gives
(γ1-γ2)^2 = (∫_{p2}^{p1} λ_p dp)^2 ≤ ∫ λ_p^2 (1-κp) dp · ∫ dp/(1-κp).
Since ∫_{p2}^{p1} dp/(1-κp) = [log(1-κp2) - log(1-κp1)]/κ, it follows that
∫∫_{T'} λ_p^2 dT ≥ ∫ (γ1-γ2)^2 κ ds / (log(1-κp2) - log(1-κp1)).
Equality holds for λ = const·log(1-κp) + const. As p1, p2 → 0 the denominator behaves like κ(p1-p2) → 0. So L → ∞ if (γ1-γ2)^2 stays above some m > 0.

This page:
(a) It finishes the sentence begun on the previous page. m need not be the smallest value of (γ1-γ2)^2, which would require that minimum to stay positive. It suffices that m be a value such that, however small δ, there are p1, p2 within δ of the line with (γ1-γ2)^2 > m. If no such m exists, γ would be continuous there. In this form the theorem is generally valid. The earlier 'minimum' form fails when γ has infinitely many maxima and minima near the line, e.g. γ ~ sin(1/p).

(b) Definition. γ is continuous at p=0 iff sup{(γ1-γ2)^2 : Π2 < p2 ≤ 0 ≤ p1 < Π1} → 0 as Π1-Π2 → 0. Hence at a discontinuity, for each s there is m > 0 such that every such window contains p1, p2 with (γ1-γ2)^2 > m. The two equalities are mutually exclusive, i.e. the window is not degenerate.

(c) Proof. Fix a strip T' with boundary values P1 > 0 > P2, and put
a = ∫ m κ ds / (log(1-κP2) - log(1-κP1)).
The aim is to show the integral can be made > C for any given C. (The draft is garbled here, but this is the intent, and it matches the print.) Because a → ∞ as P1, P2 → 0, first choose P1, P2 so that a > C. Then for each s choose p1 < P1 and p2 > P2 with (γ1-γ2)^2 > m. The denominator log(1-κp2) - log(1-κp1) = κ∫_{p2}^{p1} dp/(1-κp) decreases when the interval shrinks. Hence
∫ (γ1-γ2)^2 κ ds / (log(1-κp2) - log(1-κp1)) > a > C.
So L > C for every admissible λ with T' that thin: λ cannot approach a discontinuous γ with L bounded.

(d) A separate fragment (cf. the mapping section of the dissertation and the next page). A surface is called an image (Abbild) of another if to each point of one corresponds a definite point of the other. The image is 'zusammenhängend' (continuous) if the image point moves continuously with the varying point of the original.
errors: Slip in (b): Riemann says m can be chosen 'for every value of s'. The integral argument, however, needs m (or a positive lower bound for it) uniformly on a piece of the line of positive length. Pointwise m(s) alone does not suffice without some uniformity or measurability. The gap is unaddressed here.
Choosing p1(s), p2(s) pointwise to satisfy the inequalities can produce a T' with irregular boundary. Admissibility of such a strip (under the 'earlier restrictions') is assumed, not shown.
The monotonicity of the denominator requires 1-κp > 0 on the strip, i.e. the strip stays inside the radius of curvature. This is implicit (the previous page mentions excluding the curvature centres).
The draft's sentence structure in the 'Wird nun ...' paragraph is incomplete. The logic is recoverable and correct in substance.

results.what: Lower bound ∫∫ λ_p^2 dT ≥ ∫ (γ1-γ2)^2 κ ds/(log(1-κp2)-log(1-κp1)) across a curved strip, forcing the Dirichlet integral to blow up as the strip shrinks onto a discontinuity line
results.modern_name: Capacity/energy estimate (1D Cauchy–Schwarz / Poincaré-type) showing H^1 functions have no jump discontinuities along curves (trace argument)

results.what: Weakening the hypothesis from 'min (γ1-γ2)^2 > 0' to a limsup-type condition, motivated by the oscillatory example sin(1/p)
results.modern_name: Characterisation of discontinuity via oscillation (limsup of the jump) rather than a one-sided limit
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851 (printed Art. 17 contains the remark on m)

results.what: Definition of a surface as a (continuous) image of another

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of material printed in Riemann's 1851 dissertation (Art. 17 on the Dirichlet principle, and the mapping definition). Only the explicit sin(1/p) example and the drafting process are of minor additional interest.

transcription_corrections: The oscillating example is most likely 'sin 1/p' (in the variable p near p=0), not 'sin 1/ρ'. Both occurrences, line 6 and the end of the first paragraph, read like '1/p'.

Final paragraph should read approximately: 'Eine Fläche betrachten wir als ein Abbild einer andern, wenn jedem Punkte der einen ein bestimmter Punkt der andern entspricht, und das Abbild heißt ein zusammenhängendes, wenn der Punkt des Abbildes mit dem veränderlichen Punkte des Bildes desselben stetig fortrückt'.

In 'Die Function γ ist ... für p=0 stetig' the condition reads 'Π1 > p1 ≥ 0 und Π2 < p2 ≤ 0'. The parenthetical says the equalities exclude each other ('wo die Gleichheiten sich gegenseitig ausschließen').

'Wird nun unter den früheren Beschränkungen eine Gestalt von T' beliebig angenommen' introduces arbitrary P1, P2, with p1 < P1 and p2 > P2 chosen afterwards. The transcription's 'p1 < P1 u p2 [?]' should be 'p2 > P2'.
